thread.title: Key Words: NRA calls company backlash a ‘shameful display of public and civic cowardice’

title: Key Words: NRA calls company backlash a ‘shameful display of public and civic cowardice’

organizations.name: images barbara kollmeyer   national rifle association

text:
Published: Feb 26, 2018 7:00 a.m. ET Share 
Delta and United are the latest companies to end partnerships with the NRA Getty Images Barbara Kollmeyer Markets reporter 
The National Rifle Association has come out swinging against U.S. corporations who are ending or rethinking partnerships with the gun-rights organization, labeling them cowards and insisting its members will not be deterred from protecting their civil rights. 
Over the weekend, airlines Delta Air Lines Inc. DAL, +1.73% and United Continental Holdings Inc. UAL, +1.30% joined several companies , including a large bank and a major car-rental provider, in announcing they will drop partnerships with the NRA. The moves have come amid intense public pressure for companies to re-examine these ties after the Feb. 14 mass shooting at a Florida high school. 
In a statement on its website on Saturday , the NRA called such actions a “shameful display of political and civic cowardice.” It vowed that the brands who have abandoned it will be replaced by others who recognize that patriotism and determined commitment to Constitutional freedoms are characteristics of a marketplace they very much want to serve.” “Let it be absolutely clear. The loss of a discount will neither scare nor distract one single NRA member from our mission to stand and defend the individual freedoms that have always made America the greatest nation in the world.” National Rifle Association 
The organization said its members are not to blame for the fact that Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Fla.’s school security preparedness failed. Nor would they take the blame for “the failure of America’s mental health system, the failure of the National Instant Check System or the cruel failures of both federal and local law enforcement.” 
On Thursday, NRA Chief Executive Wayne LaPierre said those who are pushing for more gun-sale restrictions “hate the Second Amendment, they hate individual freedom.” 
Starkey Hearing Technologies became the latest to back away from the organization, announcing on its Facebook page on Sunday that it’s cutting ties, a move that elicited a mixed response from those following the company on the social-media website. 
Meanwhile, the Facebook page for Amazon.com AMZN, +0.99% is strewn with comments from users urging it to stop hosting NRA TV, amid a Twitter campaign urging people to drop their memberships until the e-commerce giant cuts those ties. Apple AAPL, +1.74% and Alphabet-owned Google’s YouTube GOOGL, +1.64% are seeing similar pressure to stop airing any streaming of NRAtv . 
Shares of gun-makers and sellers have come under pressure as well in recent days , as investment funds have also been pushed to put some distance between them and such companies. Sturm, Ruger & Co. Inc. RGR, +1.84% American Outdoor Brands Corp. AOBC, -1.19% , the parent of Smith & Wesson, were among the companies that saw pressure last week.
